hints: Expand $R\sin(x+\alpha)$ and compare its sine and cosine coefficients with $\sqrt7\sin x+2\cos x$.
Divide the coefficient equations to obtain $\tan\alpha=2/\sqrt7$, then use the required first-quadrant range for $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Expand $R\sin(x + \alpha)$ using the addition formula for sine:
$$R\sin(x + \alpha) = R(\sin x\cos\alpha + \cos x\sin\alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\sin x + (R\sin\alpha)\cos x$$

Square and add both equations to calculate $R$:
$$(R\cos\alpha)^2 + (R\sin\alpha)^2 = (\sqrt{7})^2 + 2^2$$
$$R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = 7 + 4 = 11$$
Since $R > 0$, the exact value is:
$$R = \sqrt{11}$$

Calculate $\alpha$ in the first quadrant ($0^\circ < \alpha < 90^\circ$):
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{7}}\right) \approx \tan^{-1}(0.755929) \approx 37.0869^\circ \approx 37.09^\circ$$
Thus:
$$R = \sqrt{11}, \quad \alpha = 37.09^\circ$$

hints: Use the preceding R-form with $x=2\theta$ to reduce the equation to one sine equation.
Solve $\sqrt{11}\sin(2\theta+\alpha)=1$, using the value of $\alpha$ found previously.

Because $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, solve for $2\theta+\alpha$ throughout $\alpha<2\theta+\alpha<360^\circ+\alpha$, including any valid solution just above $360^\circ$, then subtract $\alpha$ and halve.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the left-hand side of $\sqrt{7}\sin 2\theta + 2\cos 2\theta = 1$ using the R-form from part (a) with $x = 2\theta$:
$$\sqrt{11}\sin(2\theta + 37.0869^\circ) = 1$$

Divide both sides by $\sqrt{11}$ to isolate the sine term:
$$\sin(2\theta + 37.0869^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{11}}$$

Determine the range of the composite angle $\phi = 2\theta + 37.0869^\circ$. Since $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$0^\circ < 2\theta < 360^\circ$$
$$37.09^\circ < 2\theta + 37.09^\circ < 397.09^\circ$$

Calculate the principal value of the inverse sine:
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{11}}\right) \approx \sin^{-1}(0.301511) \approx 17.5484^\circ$$

Find all angles $\phi = 2\theta + 37.0869^\circ$ within the domain $(37.09^\circ, 397.09^\circ)$:
- Second quadrant angle:
$$\phi_1 = 180^\circ - 17.5484^\circ = 162.4516^\circ$$
- First quadrant angle in the next cycle ($+360^\circ$):
$$\phi_2 = 360^\circ + 17.5484^\circ = 377.5484^\circ$$
(Note that $17.5484^\circ < 37.09^\circ$, so it is outside the interval.)

Solve for $\theta$ from each valid angle:
From $\phi_1 = 162.4516^\circ$:
$$2\theta = 162.4516^\circ - 37.0869^\circ = 125.3647^\circ$$
$$\theta = \dfrac{125.3647^\circ}{2} \approx 62.68^\circ \approx 62.7^\circ$$
From $\phi_2 = 377.5484^\circ$:
$$2\theta = 377.5484^\circ - 37.0869^\circ = 340.4615^\circ$$
$$\theta = \dfrac{340.4615^\circ}{2} \approx 170.23^\circ \approx 170.2^\circ$$

State the final solutions correct to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 62.7^\circ, \quad 170.2^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Evaluates $\sin^{-1}(1/\sqrt{11})$ to at least 2 d.p. ($17.5484^\circ$). Derives $\theta=62.7^\circ$. Concludes with $\theta=62.7^\circ, 170.2^\circ$.
